title: sidecar-bridge-for-multi-tool-parallelism-and-idempotent-result-injection
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Introduce a sidecar bridging layer that coordinates parallel tool calls, provides idempotent result injection, and surface-level backpressure hints; improves stability for streaming/tool-calls and reduces duplicate side-effects.
description:
Motivation and summary: We see frequent customer patterns where a single LLM response triggers multiple external tool invocations in parallel (search, db-read, external API). The previous model of allowing callers to fan-out directly produced several operational problems: duplicate side-effects on retries, unpredictable ordering of injected tool results, and poor streaming stability when downstream tool latencies spiked. This PR introduces a lightweight per-request sidecar bridge that acts as an execution coordinator for multi-tool calls. Goals: 1) Provide idempotent result injection so model output receives a stable, deterministic sequence of tool results even across retries and hedges. 2) Surface backpressure and capacity hints so the serving runtime can gracefully degrade (fallback to synchronous tooling, model-only responses) when tool fanout exceeds configured budgets. 3) Improve streaming stability by buffering and ordering tool-result commits and streaming partials to the client with clear markers.

What changed (high level): - New sidecar bridge component (sidecar/bridge package) that maintains per-request coordination state, idempotency keys, and result-merge policies. - Extended tool-caller API surface to accept idempotency_key and preferred_injection_order metadata. - Added a light-weight backpressure protocol: Bridge emits X-Bridge-Backpressure headers and exposes a health endpoint used by the runtime scheduler. - Structured-output adapter that merges tool returns into the model's structured output (openai-compatible shape) deterministically; added contract tests. - Documentation and SDK glue in redwood-sdk-typescript for the new opt-in surface.

Commit summary: - 3a9f2b4: introduce sidecar bridge scaffold, coordinator state machine and unit tests. - b78c11d: implement idempotency key handling, persisted request metadata and replay protection. - c44e5f1: backpressure headers, health probe and runtime hooks. - e12b9d0: structured output merger and OpenAI-compat adapter. - f9b7a84: SDK examples, docs and e2e contract tests. - 9c2d4a5: polish: logging, metrics, and comments from review.

Files changed (illustrative): - sidecar/bridge/bridge.go (core coordinator state machine, 420 lines) - sidecar/bridge/idempotency.go (idempotency store + TTL logic) - sidecar/bridge/merge_policy.go (ordered/priority merging strategies) - runtime/router/bridge_integration.go (runtime hooks to consult backpressure and health) - runtime/streaming/ordered_stream.go (buffered streaming with markers) - sdk/typescript/examples/multi_tool_sidecar.ts (example wiring) - docs/api/sidecar.md (integration guide & compatibility notes) - tests/integration/sidecar_e2e_test.go (end-to-end tests) - ci/workflows/sidecar_contract.yml (new CI job that runs contract tests) - telemetry/metrics/bridge_metrics.prom (metrics defs)

Design notes and tradeoffs: - The bridge is intentionally opt-in per request. We do not force all tool-calls through it because some low-latency, in-process tool calls would add unnecessary hops. - Idempotency is based on a user-provided idempotency_key or computed hash; replay protection TTL is configurable. This avoids double-application of side-effects even when retries are transparent in the runtime. - Merge policies support: ordered (strict injection by the order provided), priority (tool-level priority), and first-success (first non-error result wins). Default is ordered to preserve deterministic behavior for model evals. - Backpressure is advisory: runtime scheduler can choose to fallback to synchronous tool invocation or use smaller fanout windows. This reduces tail latency impact on streaming responses.

Backward compatibility and OpenAI compat: - The structured-output adapter emits an OpenAI-compatible tools field and enumerates injections as choices/named objects so existing OpenAI-compat clients see a predictable shape. - The SDK additions are marked experimental and behind a feature flag (ENABLE_SIDECAR_BRIDGE).

Review conversation (highlights, chronological): - Marta Iqbal (review): "Great approach. Two asks: (1) Can we make the default TTL for idempotency conservative (30s+) and configurable via runtime config? (2) Add a safety check preventing persistent side-effects from running through the bridge by accident?" - Author (Avery): "Set default TTL to 2 minutes and added a per-tool allow_side_effect boolean; runtime will fail-fast if a tool marked side_effect=true is attempted via sidecar without explicit opt-in." - Diego Ramos (review): "Ordered merge looks good but concerned about large buffering causing memory pressure. Can we limit buffer size and switch to streaming partial results beyond a threshold?" - Author: "Added a `max_buffered_results` config and fallback behavior to stream with 'partial_injection' markers; included tests for the threshold case." - Zoe Patel (review): "CI flaked on contract suite first run; please stabilize tests for race windows." - Author: "Tightened test timings and added retries in the contract pipeline; re-ran CI." - Final approvals: Marta and Diego approved after the follow-ups.

CI and validation: - New CI job sidecar_contract.yml runs integration against a local runtime stub and the SDK example. - Initial run failed due to a race in the idempotency TTL eviction test (flake). Fixed by using deterministic fake clock in tests and re-ran. - All status checks green on merge: build, unit-tests, integration, contract-tests, lint, gosec. - CI summary: build/pass, unit-test/pass, integration/pass, contract-tests/pass, lint/pass.

Safety and rollout plan: - Behind feature flag ENABLE_SIDECAR_BRIDGE for server-side and SDK. - Canary rollout on Dedicated customers for a week with telemetry dashboards (bridge_requests_total, bridge_backpressure_events, bridge_replay_protections). - Watch for increased 5xx from tool adapters and elevated backpressure events; automated rollback policy if error budget exceeded.

Migration notes for consumers: - Opt-in by passing `sidecar: { enabled: true, idempotency_key: "...", merge_policy: "ordered" }` in the tool-call envelope (example in docs). - When migrating existing multi-tool orchestrations, enable allow_side_effect for side-effecting tools only after manual review.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merged by Avery Chen on 2026-02-25 after approvals. Commit message summarizes feature and calls out the two follow-up tickets created: ENG-1487 (telemetry refinements), ENG-1499 (sdk ergonomics polishing).
